# Fuel Blends {#sec-fuel-blends}

Technologies in CIMS rarely request a pure fuel. They request a blend, and the blend's makeup decides the fuel's cost and lifecycle emissions. Each sector's Service sub-tree carries one **Fuel Blend** node for each blended fuel it uses, and the sector's technologies request fuel from those nodes. When renewable content in a blend rises, the carbon intensity of every technology that burns the blend falls with it, without any change to the technologies themselves.

## Blend nodes

| Blend | What it blends | Sectors |
|:------|:---------------|:--------|
| Methane | Natural gas with biogas, gas from biomass gasification, renewable natural gas, and hydrogen | Every sector except Construction, Direct Air Capture, and Forestry |
| Diesel | Fossil diesel with biodiesel and renewable diesel | Every sector except Construction, Direct Air Capture, Forestry, Residential, and Waste |
| Gasoline | Fossil gasoline with ethanol | Natural Gas, Petroleum Crude, and both transportation sectors |
| Still gas | Refinery fuel gas produced by the refinery's own units | Petroleum Crude and Petroleum Refining |
| Process gas | Blast-furnace, coke-oven, and basic oxygen furnace gases | Iron and Steel |

: Fuel blend nodes {#tbl-fuel-blends}

The first three are true blends: they mix a purchased fossil fuel with lower-carbon substitutes supplied by the Biofuels and Hydrogen sectors (see @sec-biodiesel, @sec-ethanol, and @sec-hydrogen). The last two route a sector's own by-product fuels to the steam, reheating, and direct-heat nodes that burn them; the heat they provide is counted at those nodes.

The technology database does not describe the blending technologies; their shares and limits come from the CIMS model inputs.
